page1.title: What is context?
page1.subtitle: Earlier words and tokens provide clues for what might come next.
page1.question: What is context?
page1.intro: LLMs do not work with one word in isolation. They can use the words or tokens that came before to help predict what might come next.
page1.definition: Context is information from the earlier text or tokens that the model can use.
page1.takeawayLead: The words before a token give it context.
page1.takeaway: Context can change what the model predicts next.
page1.thinkIntro: Which word is more likely to come next in each sentence? This is a quick exploration, not a scored quiz.
page1.promptA: I went to the bank to deposit some
page1.promptB: We sat by the bank of the
page1.correctFeedback: That fits! The earlier words make this the most likely choice.
page1.wrongFeedback: Not quite. Look at the earlier words for the strongest clue, then try again.

page2.title: What is a context window?
page2.subtitle: A context window sets the amount of text available for the current prediction.
page2.question: What is a context window?
page2.introLead: An LLM cannot use unlimited text at once.
page2.intro: The amount of text or tokens it can work with at one time is called its
page2.visualTitle: Imagine a long story as a line of tokens.
page2.visualIntro: The model can use the tokens inside its context window for the current prediction.
page2.sequenceLabel: A long token sequence with the current context window highlighted
page2.windowLabel: Context window — what the model can use
page2.definition: The amount of text or tokens the model can use at one time.
page2.differentSizes: Different models can have different context-window sizes.
page2.takeaway: If text is outside the window, it may not be available to the model for the current prediction.
page2.sizesIntro: Some models can work with more tokens at once than others.

page3.title: Why does context matter?
page3.subtitle: Different earlier context can change next-token probabilities.
page3.question: Why does context matter?
page3.intro: The words before a blank can change which next tokens are more likely.
page3.compareIntro: The last part is the same, but the earlier context is different.
page3.illustrative: Illustrative teaching example — not live model measurements.
page3.leadA: The cat was chasing the mouse.
page3.leadB: The mouse was looking for cheese.
page3.sameEnding: The last words are identical. Only the earlier context is different.
page3.differentChances: Because the context differs, the model assigns different probabilities to possible next tokens.
page3.keyIdeaText: Context changes which next tokens are more likely.
page3.summary: Same ending, different context → different predictions.
page3.summaryNote: This is why context matters for an LLM.

page4.title: What if the context gets too long?
page4.subtitle: A long input can extend beyond the context available for the current prediction.
page4.question: What if the context gets too long?
page4.introLead: The text you provide might be longer than the model’s context window.
page4.intro: The model can only use the tokens available inside its current context window.
page4.topInfo: Information outside the window may not be available for the current next-token prediction.
page4.windowLabel: Context window — what the model can use
page4.visualTitle: Imagine a very long token sequence.
page4.visualIntro: Only a small part of it is inside the context window right now.
page4.sequenceLabel: A long token sequence with the currently available context highlighted
page4.sequenceTokens: Once upon a time there a little reader who loved to learn new things every day in a far away land
page4.windowNote: Only these tokens are used now
page4.sizesTitle: Different models have different context-window sizes.
page4.sizesNote: Some can handle more tokens at once; some can handle fewer.
page4.sizesExpanded: Different models can support different context-window sizes. A larger window means more tokens can be available at once; it does not mean the model is more intelligent or always more accurate.

page5.title: Context window in action
page5.subtitle: Move and resize the window, then observe how the model's next-token probabilities change.
page5.question: Try it yourself: the context window in action!
page5.introLead: Move the window to see which tokens are available to the model right now.
page5.intro: Only the tokens inside the window can be used for the next prediction.
page5.guide: Drag the window or use the buttons to move it.
page5.step1Note: This is the full text, shown as tokens, that you provide to the model.
page5.sequenceLabel: A long token sequence with a movable context window
page5.sequenceTokens: Once upon a time there was a curious little reader who loved to learn new things every day in a far away land
page5.windowLabel: CONTEXT WINDOW (what the model can use)
page5.step2Note: Move the window to see how the available context changes.
page5.availableNote: These tokens are available to the model for the next prediction.
page5.predictionsNote: Based only on the available context, the model gives these tokens the highest probabilities next.
page5.realModelLabel: Top 5 from the real language model
page5.summaryLead: Only the tokens inside the current context window are available for this prediction.

page6.title: Check the idea
page6.subtitle: Four quick questions to check the key ideas about context.
page6.quickQuestions: 4 quick questions to see what you remember.
page6.answerEach: Answer each question, then check your answer.
page6.completionText: You’ve checked the key ideas about context.
page6.completedIdea1: Context is the earlier information the model can use
page6.completedIdea2: The context window limits how much context is available at one time
page6.completedIdea3: Changing context can change next-token predictions
page6.completedIdea4: Text outside the current usable window may not be available for that prediction
page6.q1A: The final answer the model gives.
page6.q1B: The earlier text or tokens the model can use when making a prediction.
page6.q1C: The training data used to build the model.
page6.q1D: The list of all possible tokens.
page6.q1Correct: Exactly! Context is the earlier text or tokens available to the model when it works out what may come next.
page6.q1Incorrect: Not quite. Think about the text or tokens that are already available before the next prediction is made.
page6.q2A: The amount of text or tokens the model can use at one time.
page6.q2B: A picture showing the model’s answer.
page6.q2C: All the text the model has ever been trained on.
page6.q2D: A score showing how important a token is.
page6.q2Correct: Right! A context window is the amount of text or tokens the model can use at one time.
page6.q2Incorrect: Try again. Remember the token window you moved in the activity.
page6.q3Prompt: Why can changing the context change the next-token prediction?
page6.q3A: The model chooses a different answer randomly.
page6.q3B: Different context gives the model different information to use for the prediction.
page6.q3C: Changing context changes the model’s training data.
page6.q3D: The model always predicts the same token anyway.
page6.q3Correct: Exactly! Different context gives the model different information, so different next tokens can become more or less likely.
page6.q3Incorrect: Think about the prediction bars in the context activity. What changed when the available context changed?
page6.q4Prompt: What can happen when the text is longer than the model’s current context window?
page6.q4A: The model can always use every token at the same time.
page6.q4B: Some text outside the current usable window may not be available for that prediction.
page6.q4Correct: Correct! The model can only use the context available inside its current usable window for that prediction.
page6.q4Incorrect: Not quite. Text outside the current usable window is not necessarily deleted — it may simply not be available for that prediction.

page7.title: Lesson summary
page7.subtitle: Context determines which earlier tokens are available and can influence what the model predicts next.
page7.idea2Copy: The context window limits what the model can use.
page7.idea3Copy: Only information inside the current window may be available.
page7.idea4Copy: Different context can change next-token probabilities.
page7.recap: Context helps the model use earlier information when deciding what might come next.
page7.next: Now that we know which tokens are available, Lesson 3 explores how information can be combined between them.
